editorial.summary: TigerBelly's 300th episode begins with preserved pre-roll conflict about microphones, artwork, nudity and a Lord of the Rings humility metaphor before formally crediting DVDASA as an influence on TigerBelly. David Choe and the cast compare memories of meeting Bobby Lee, debate why Choe and Lee are not closer friends, revisit an unmade shared handcuff-show concept, discuss Steve Lee, recovery, bereavement, reported ADHD, family violence, treatment, EMDR wall-punching and the unsafe idea that artistic framing can bypass clinical constraints. Choe says he rehearsed more than twenty hours of provocative TigerBelly material and repeatedly vetoed it because it felt harmful. Steven Yeun enters for a planned affirmation of Lee's Asian-American influence, leading into MADtv workplace history, Khalyla's nursing and relationship labor, Korean and Filipino representation, self-production, role refusal, Star Wars chronology and an anonymous eighteen-year-old's question about mental health versus art. The episode directly rejects suffering and suicidality as requirements for creativity. Every idea, dispute, joke, self-correction and publisher mask remains. Corrections, privacy, consent, health, labor and attribution are separate metadata. No named line-level turns are published.
